narrative:
The model determined that you have a 41% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough for the bank to consider you too risky, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were, in order: the status of your checking account, your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income, and the length of the loan you requested. 

Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This made the bank view you as higher risk.

Your requested installment rate of 2% of disposable income worked in your favor, pulling the prediction toward approval. It is lower than the 3% average among those who were approved, which the model saw as a positive.

The 12-month duration you asked for also helped your case, as it is shorter than the 19-month average among approved loans. Shorter loans are generally viewed more favorably.

Unfortunately, the negative effect from your checking account status outweighed these positive signals. 

You should focus on building a positive checking account balance, then reapply once your account consistently shows funds rather than a deficit. This single change would likely improve your chances significantly. (218 words)
